1.explanation: The Nav class in nav.jsx is responsible for rendering the sliding tab list and controlling its scroll behavior. componentDidMount (and potentially componentDidUpdate) is where event listeners for drag and keyboard should be initialized. initialSettings likely sets up initial offsets and state for slide mode. setOffset and _adjustTarget compute and apply the scroll offset when the active tab changes or when the user scrolls; these methods must handle drag deltas. setSlideBtn controls the visibility/enable state of the navigation arrows based on current offset. To support dragging and keyboard navigation, these methods need to be extended to listen for pointer/mouse/touch events in componentDidMount/initialSettings, calculate drag movement in setOffset/_adjustTarget, and update the arrow states in setSlideBtn accordingly.
1.bug_scenario: In slide mode, when the total width of tabs exceeds the container, the overflow arrows appear but the user cannot drag the tab list itself to scroll. The screenshots show a long row of tabs with left/right arrow buttons, but dragging (mouse‐drag) or using keyboard to scroll the hidden tabs does not work, making it inconvenient to reach tabs outside the visible area.

2.explanation: The Nav class in nav.jsx is responsible for calculating and applying the horizontal offset of the tab list (in its setOffset and _adjustTarget methods) and for updating the slide buttons (in setSlideBtn). componentDidMount and componentWillUnmount currently handle mounting logic (including binding/unbinding events) but do not register any drag or keyboard listeners. To support mouse dragging or keyboard scrolling, you must extend Nav (in componentDidMount/unmount) to listen for mousedown/touchstart/keydown events, then call setOffset (bounded via _adjustTarget) as the user drags or presses arrow keys. Updating these methods will directly address the missing scroll interactions for overflowed tabs.
2.bug_scenario: In slide mode, when the total width of tabs exceeds the container, users can only click the left/right arrow buttons to scroll the tab list. The user expected to be able to drag the tab bar with the mouse or use keyboard arrow keys to scroll it. In the provided screenshot, the overflow tabs (e.g. “More 1”, “More 2”) cannot be dragged horizontally, making navigation inconvenient.
